summary: This chunk is a diff adding a new file, report.md, for an adversarial review of a follow-the-sun on-call rotation plan. Three fresh-eyes adversaries merged twelve raw findings into eight, none killed. Findings cover an uncovered 6-hour nightly paging gap (F1), Sev1s stalling on a sleeping US incident commander (F2), go-live gated by calendar rather than access provisioning (F3), a too-short training ramp (F4), a fragile 3-person rotation (F5), a dead-ending escalation chain (F6), a perverse success metric (F7), and unvalidated runbooks (F8). Three verification items and a retest list follow.

claims.text: Twelve raw findings from three adversaries were merged into eight, with none killed.
No finding is graded Critical because every failure is recoverable; F4 would become Critical if verification item V1 confirms destructive runbook branches exist.
F1: the Krakow (08:00-20:00 CET) and US-East (02:00-14:00 ET / 08:00-20:00 ET) windows leave 20:00-02:00 ET uncovered daily, with 'closest' undefined as a routing rule.
F2: the entire incident-commander pool is US-based with no overnight IC schedule, so Sev1s during Krakow's shift lack a reachable IC.
F3: go-live is scheduled 'starting next month' with no gate on access provisioning, which is still 'in progress' per the plan's own notes.
F4: a single shadow week does not guarantee exposure to any real incidents and has no reverse-shadow (Krakow-drives, US-watches) phase.
F5: the 3-person Krakow rotation covers 12h/7d with no secondary layer or minimum-staffing threshold, versus an industry floor of 4-6 for a sustainable single-site rotation.
F6: the escalation chain has exactly one hop and no terminal fallback, so two consecutive missed acks leave a Sev1 unacknowledged indefinitely.
F7: the success metric (zero overnight pages to US-East) is defined so that legitimate overnight escalations under step 4 count as metric failures, pressuring Krakow engineers to suppress escalation.
F8: runbook readiness is defined only as 'tidy them up,' with no completion criterion and no validation by a non-author reader.

risks.note: F1's corroboration cites '~42 hours/week' of overnight paging absorbed silently, with no computation or source shown in this chunk.
F5's root cause asserts an 'industry floor for a sustainable single-site rotation is 4-6' with no citation.
The claim that twelve raw findings were merged into exactly eight, with none killed, is stated without showing the original twelve or the merge reasoning in this chunk.
All findings are assessed against 'oncall-rotation-plan.md' and 'charter.md', neither of which appears in this chunk, so severity and status labels cannot be checked against the source artifact here.

least_confident: Whether F1's, F5's, and F7's severity/status labels (e.g. 'Confirmed', 'High') are justified cannot be checked here because the underlying oncall-rotation-plan.md and charter.md are not part of this chunk.
